name: eventfd
synopsis: int eventfd(unsigned int initval, int flags);
description: eventfd() creates an eventfd object for event notification between user-space applications and the kernel. It initializes a 64-bit unsigned integer counter with the specified initial value and returns a file descriptor to access it.

parameters.name: flags
parameters.description: Flags to modify behavior, such as EFD_CLOEXEC for close-on-exec, EFD_NONBLOCK for non-blocking operation, or EFD_SEMAPHORE for semaphore-like semantics.

return_value.success: Returns a new eventfd file descriptor
return_value.failure: Returns -1 on error, and errno is set to indicate the error

errors.description: An unsupported value was specified in flags.
The per-process limit on the number of open file descriptors has been reached.
The system-wide limit on the total number of open files has been reached.
Could not mount (internal) anonymous inode device.
There was insufficient memory to create a new eventfd file descriptor.

examples: switch (fork()) { case 0: /* Child process writes to efd */ for (...) { write(efd, &u, sizeof(uint64_t)); } exit(EXIT_SUCCESS); default: /* Parent reads from efd */ read(efd, &u, sizeof(uint64_t)); }
